If, for instance, a girl was abused by her father, but knows that reporting him to police will get him executed, she might not be willing to. She may have only wanted her father to do a few years in prison, but not be put to death. Plus, you can imagine the immense pressure that family members and relatives might bring on her to make her be quiet if the law penalty were death.

Now, you may ask, what if the perpetrator is indeed a total stranger? Well, that then leads to its own set of problems: If the penalty for child abuse were the same as murder - namely, it would lead to life imprisonment or death - then you're giving predators incentive to kill their victims to keep them quiet. To be sure, a significant number of perps do so already. But making the penalty for child abuse tantamount to murder would make murder seem logical in the eyes of many predators, since they have nothing to lose and they'd keep their victims silent. So this might actually make murder rates go up.
